transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-04
Time: 15:00 PT / 22:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Solace Head of Data), Carlos (Solace Security), Alyssa (Solace PM)

[00:00] Jasmine: hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick intro, i'm jasmine from Redwood, ethan my teammate is our solutions engineer, we'll run through how we handle pii and retention for pilot, and gather your success criteria.
[00:18] Priya: hi thanks, i'll kick off. we're scoping a 4-week POC to evaluate using redwood for clinical note summarization. main concern is pii—patient names, MRNs, dates—can't leave our systems in cleartext. also need clear retention and audit for compliance.
[00:34] Ethan: got it. quick question, when you say "can't leave in cleartext" do you mean you need prompts never logged, or that logs need to be redacted?
[00:41] Priya: both, ideally. for our sensitive routes we want logging disabled, and for other routes we want automatic redaction of PHI before storage. must be able to define field-level rules.
[00:51] Carlos: and encryption at rest with our KMS—HSM-backed key, plus access audit logs. also SSO for users.
[00:58] Jasmine: yea those are all standard asks. to be explicit: Redwood supports route-level logging controls, per-route retention TTLs, and a purge API. we integrate with customer KMS for envelope keys, and we have SOC 2 and ISO docs—i'll share.
[01:12] Priya: can you explain how redaction works in practice? is it client-side or server-side?
[01:16] Ethan: good q. two patterns: 1) client-side pre-processing — you run a stripper before sending and send only tokenized placeholders. 2) server-side redaction — Redwood can apply regex/NER pipelines to mask PII before logs are persisted. server-side gives easier ops but we offer client libs to do local redaction if you need zero-touch logging.
[01:36] Alyssa: do you store the original prompt anywhere? we've seen vendors keep full prompts for debugging.
[01:41] Ethan: by default, we persist request/response for 30 days for debugging, but you can disable retention per-route. for the POC we can set the clinical route to "no persistence" and enable a minimal trace id only. so original prompts won't be stored.
[01:55] Carlos: what's minimal trace id—does it contain any identifying info?
[01:59] Ethan: just a UUID and timestamp, no payload. it's used to map logs across services when needed.
[02:05] Priya: ok. what about prompt storage in model cache or kv cache on the GPU nodes—does that persist beyond the request?
[02:12] Ethan: runtime notes: the KV cache is ephemeral per session and lives in GPU memory, it is not written to disk. once the session ends it's reclaimed. however for streaming and long-running chats there's an in-memory cache; we don't persist that unless you enable conversation storage.
[02:28] Priya: any chance model providers or third parties see prompts?
[02:32] Jasmine: no, for private/dedicated deployments Redwood doesn't send data to third-party hosts. for Redwood hosted, we route only to the models in our catalog; we also support bringing-your-own-model in your VPC for full isolation.
[02:44] Carlos: about retention and legal hold, can we set different retention per customer and have an emergency purge?
[02:50] Ethan: yes. retention is per-route and per-tenant. we have APIs for purge and restores. legal hold is supported—if you set a legal_hold flag we keep data and mark it non-purgeable.
[03:01] Priya: audit logs—who accessed what and when?
[03:04] Jasmine: we emit audit logs to your configured cloud storage or SIEM. logs include request metadata, route, user id, and action. we can redact request/response bodies from audit export if required.
[03:17] Alyssa: good. now on redaction accuracy—we need NER that catches MRNs and custom identifiers. is it rule-based or ML?
[03:24] Ethan: both. we have built-in NER models for names, dates, IDs, plus you can add custom regex matchers and a custom entity list for Solace-specific identifiers. some customers preprocess with their own anonymizer for 100% coverage.
[03:38] Priya: for the POC we can ship a seed list of MRN patterns. can you support mapping replaced tokens back to original for debugging when stored only under secure keys?
[03:47] Ethan: yes, we support reversible tokenization if you enable "secure re-identification" and store keys in your KMS. that's an opt-in enterprise feature and comes with strict audit controls.
[03:58] Carlos: encryption details—TDE at rest plus envelope encryption with customer KMS. can you confirm HSM integration and key rotation?
[04:06] Jasmine: we support AWS KMS, Google KMS, and external HSM via the KMIP interface; rotation and key policies follow your KMS capabilities. we'll include details in the security pack.
[04:16] Priya: great. ok benchmarks—what do you need from us to run a representative load test?
[04:21] Ethan: sample size and distribution: we'd like a payload sample of ~1k requests across short (1-2 prompts), medium (3-5 prompts), and long (10+ prompts) sequences. also target concurrency—what qps do you expect?
[04:33] Priya: starting pilot will be low qps, maybe 5-10 concurrent, but production target is 200 qps for summarization pipelines.
[04:40] Ethan: we'll run both latency SLO tests (p99/median) and tokenized cost estimates. for the POC we can simulate 10 concurrent and run a sustained 1k-request pass to measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:53] Alyssa: timeline—we had hoped to start in two weeks. is that feasible?
[04:57] Jasmine: yes, if we get your sample data and decisions on logging/retention we can spin up a pilot instance and run benchmarks within 1 week.
[05:04] Priya: accept. what success criteria should we sign off on?
[05:07] Jasmine: common success criteria: <1s median latency for short prompts, p99 under 2.5s for typical workloads, automatic redaction accuracy above 98% on seeded MRNs/names, and confirmation that no raw prompts are persisted for clinical routes.
[05:20] Priya: sounds good. can you capture acceptance tests? we want: 1) benchmark report, 2) redaction sample pass with our examples, 3) security docs and pilot contract.
[05:31] Jasmine: noted. we'll deliver that.
[05:33] Ethan: quick note—if you want absolute zero logging we can also offer a dedicated private deployment in your VPC; that takes longer to stand up but meets highest isolation.
[05:44] Carlos: timeline/cost tradeoff?
[05:46] Ethan: dedicated adds provisioning lead time, typically 4-6 weeks and an infra commitment. pilot on hosted with route-level no-persist is the fastest path.
[05:55] Priya: from compliance perspective hosted with no-persist plus KMS and audit logs is acceptable for the pilot; production may move to private.
[06:04] Jasmine: ok i'll send SOC2/security pack and pilot pricing. Ethan will run the benchmark.
[06:09] Alyssa: any blockers on our side? Priya: we'll send example prompts and list of PHI fields.
[06:14] Jasmine: recap and next steps then.
[06:17] Ethan: action items: benchmark run, confirm KMS details, set route retention to zero for clinical route, implement regex for MRN.
[06:25] Jasmine: we'll follow up with calendar invite for 8/13 to review results. thanks everyone.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings; some technical terms transcribed inconsistently (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes as "K V cache").

References shared during call:
- Redwood security pack (link sent after call)
- Benchmark plan spreadsheet (SE to create)
- Example redaction regex templates

Recap (as said on call):
- Pilot length: 4 weeks; immediate POC on hosted with route-level no-persist and KMS integration.
- Success criteria: latency SLO targets, >98% redaction accuracy on seeded tests, no raw prompt persistence for clinical route.
- Deliverables: security docs, pilot pricing, benchmark report, redaction sample results.

End of transcript.
